title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: Hold: the briefing treats licensing and metering as wholly unpublished even though Copilot Studio documents baseline Copilot Credits billing and a conditional Microsoft 365 Copilot inclusion. The label-encryption instructions also omit a required wizard step and the PowerShell reference's conditions for configuring encryption rights.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; summary; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the common currency across Copilot Studio capabilities. You can get them through pay-as-you-go meters, prepurchase plans, and Copilot Credit prepaid pack subscriptions.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to mixed. Replace the notes and unqualified licensing-gap sentences with: 'Existing Copilot Studio licensing and Copilot Credits rules apply to agent usage. Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users' classic answers, generative answers and Microsoft Graph tenant grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged when the agent runs with their authenticated identity. claims.claim: No separate tenant or agent switch for the planned labelled-file support is documented.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Makers enable existing per-agent file input at Settings > Generative AI > File processing capabilities > File uploads.
claims.quote: Go to the Settings page for your agent, and select Generative AI. Navigate to the File processing capabilities section. Turn on File uploads.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the existing File uploads setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio File uploads API Dataverse; File uploads botcomponent setting API; File uploads Power Platform API PowerShell; File uploads bot Web API. Read image-input-analysis and pac copilot search excerpt; no File uploads setting operation found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained how the planned labelled-file support interacts with the existing File uploads setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio sensitivity labels uploads default; Copilot Studio Purview Information Protection labelled file upload support Microsoft 365 channel prerequisites opt in. Opened image-input-analysis and ai-copilot-studio; no planned-feature setting interaction was stated.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP location is reached through Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: The printed New-DLPCompliancePolicy and New-DLPComplianceRule calls create the Copilot policy and blocking rule after $loc and $advrule are defined.
claims.quote:
New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")
New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The rule uses Content contains > Sensitivity labels to exclude labelled items from processing.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented label-based Copilot DLP control covers Copilot Studio agents when the knowledge source is SharePoint.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: DLP does not scan file contents uploaded directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Label-based Copilot DLP coverage of the planned Copilot Studio agent uploads is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files sensitivity labels EXTRACT identity permissions downstream connectors label protection check. Opened ai-copilot-studio and dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about; agent coverage states SharePoint knowledge, not the planned labelled uploads.

claims.claim: The label-encryption wizard path is create or edit a sensitivity label > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: Then, on the Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected page, make sure you select Control access. ... On the Access control page, select one of the following options
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'create or edit a sensitivity label > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now'. Retain https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <rights> configures label encryption permissions without specifying the encryption mode.
claims.quote: This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.
claims.fix: For the documented admin-defined encryption configuration, replace the call in both places with 'Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionEnabled $true -EncryptionProtectionType Template -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <rights>'. Add to the note: 'This call enables template-based encryption with admin-defined rights; it is not the user-defined-permissions configuration.' Retain the Set-Label reference.

claims.claim: The EXTRACT permission is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.where: controls[3].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The person applying encryption is the Rights Management owner and always has EXTRACT, regardless of restrictions configured for other people.
claims.quote: The person applying the encryption always has the EXTRACT usage right, because they are the Rights Management owner. This special role automatically includes all usage rights and some other actions

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: For the documented label-encryption scenarios, AI apps require VIEW and EXTRACT to return protected data.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.claim: The portal route for enabling SharePoint and OneDrive label support is Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. ... If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables the documented SharePoint and OneDrive label-processing capabilities.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: Enabling label support through the portal requires a global administrator.
claims.quote: This option is the easiest way to enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive. You must sign in as a global administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must use PowerShell to enable the capabilities.
claims.quote: If you have Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must use PowerShell to enable these capabilities for all your geo-locations.

claims.claim: Purview recommends enabling sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: If you haven't already, we recommend you enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive and also familiarize yourself with the file types and label configurations that these services can process.

claims.claim: Without enabling that support, encrypted files accessible to Copilot and agents are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.
claims.quote: When sensitivity labels aren't enabled for these services, the encrypted files that Copilot and agents can access are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.

claims.claim: The monitoring report is at Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) > Reports > Copilot experiences & agents.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) ... navigate to the Reports page to view the results of your policy. Select Copilot experiences & agents

claims.claim: That report monitors sensitive agent interactions rather than enforcing a processing block.
claims.quote: Select Copilot experiences & agents and view information such as: ... Sensitive interactions per AI app ... Potential risky AI usage

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to wait at least a day for policy data before viewing report results.
claims.quote: Wait at least a day for data, and then navigate to the Reports page to view the results of your policy.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for this DSPM for AI report is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DSPM Copilot experiences reports API; DSPM for AI reports Graph API export. Opened ai-copilot-studio; read dspm-for-ai and developer/testconfiguration search excerpts. No API for this report was documented; generic Audit and eDiscovery retrieval are different operations.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Current standard-harness file-input documentation says encrypted files, including sensitivity-labelled or password-protected files, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: An encrypted Office upload produces an encrypted/password-protected message or, for some rights-managed files, a generic error.
claims.quote: the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read. For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The cited file-input article applies to agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The article directs readers to Microsoft Copilot Chat as an experience supporting labelled files.
claims.quote: use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels expose an agent in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing: conflicting SharePoint encryption documentation
claims.claim: The SharePoint troubleshooting article says agents cannot ground on file content protected by encryption.
claims.quote: the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.claim: User-defined-permission encryption limits access to unopened SharePoint and OneDrive files.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: The documented exceptions are default labels extending SharePoint permissions and files referenced with '/', both requiring EXTRACT.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to the planned labelled-upload support have not been documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Purview Information Protection labelled file upload support Microsoft 365 channel prerequisites opt in. Opened image-input-analysis and ai-copilot-studio; neither states prerequisites for the planned protected-upload feature.

claims.claim: The feature itself takes no action and all action risk comes from write-capable tools on the same agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio labelled file uploads automatic actions autonomy. Read the roadmap, image-input-analysis and guidance/pass-files-to-connectors. They describe processing and optional downstream flows, not a complete guarantee that this planned feature takes no action.
